title: Grove throttles each conduit's inflow and outflow through separate on-chain RateLimitIDs, so deposits and withdrawals are governed independently
content:
Every Instance in this chunk declares its rate limits as *pairs* of opaque on-chain identifiers. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.10.1.2.3 states that "the specific `RateLimitID`(s) for this conduit's inflow and outflow are defined in the subdocuments herein," and the subdocuments then give one hash for inflow (e.g. `0x1fd0baaf…`) and a separate one for outflow (`0x786ff17c…`).

Directional separation is the load-bearing detail. Because the limit is keyed by direction, capacity consumed on the way in cannot deplete capacity on the way out. Filling a deposit bucket does not impair Grove's ability to unwind the position, and conversely governance can set an inflow limit to zero — freezing new exposure to a venue — without touching the exit path.

The identifiers are content-addressed hashes rather than human-readable names, which means the Atlas text is the only mapping from a governance intent ("the Agora AUSD deposit limit") to the on-chain slot it controls. That makes the configuration document itself a piece of critical infrastructure: an error in the recorded hash silently retargets a governance change at the wrong conduit.

A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.12.3.2.3 extends the same pattern to a third direction — swaps get their own RateLimitIDs alongside deposit and withdrawal — confirming that the axis is *operation type*, not merely in/out.
description: Each Instance registers distinct inflow and outflow rate-limit hashes, so an exhausted deposit budget never blocks exits and a closed inflow can coexist with an open outflow.
